paper.subject: geography
paper.title: 14th International Geography Olympiad — Fieldwork Exercise 2 — Sustainable development of youth tourism at Košutnjak Park of Belgrade, Serbia

documentNotes.title: INSTRUCTIONS
documentNotes.statement:
All tasks must be completed individually, using the answer templates provided.
The Resource Booklet contains important supporting materials: tables with statistical data, maps, etc.

**Time management:**

You have **10 minutes** to read the tasks and Resource Booklet. No writing during this time.
Students with English as the language of instruction then have **2 hours** to complete the test.
All other students have **2 hours and 20 minutes**.

Write your answers **in pen**.
You may use colored pencils/pens for map work.
You may refer to material in the Resource Booklet in your answers, and you may use material included in earlier answers to the FWE-1 you have provided.

**Total marks for FWE-2: 20**

paper.caveat: The tasks refer to Table 1 and Maps 4, 5 and 6 of a separate Resource Booklet, which is not part of this document.

transcription.notes: Answer booklet of Fieldwork Exercise 2 (FWE-2), 9 pages. Page 1 is the cover (iGeo logo, Belgrade coat of arms, student-number boxes) and page 2 the instructions, kept in paper.documentNotes; the printed total is 20 marks. Eight numbered tasks I.1–IV.2 are the eight problems, matching the inventory; marks as printed: 1, 1, 2, 2+1, 5, 1, 4, 3 (sum 20). II.2 prints two questions with separate marks (2 m) and (1 m); the second is unlabelled, so both stay in the statement and the problem carries 3. IV.1 has labelled sub-questions A., B., C. with no separate marks. The time limit of 120 minutes is for students with English as the language of instruction (others have 2 hours 20 minutes), plus 10 minutes reading time. The answer boxes ('Place for calculations', 'Answer') and ruled answer lines are not transcribed except the printed field labels; answer tables are given as Markdown tables with their printed headers. Map Template 1 (page 6, landscape) is cropped as a figure; its legend table is transcribed in III.1. In IV.2 the scale labels are printed rotated in the first column. Printed as is: II.1 opens a parenthesis '(Map 6 of the Resource booklet.' without closing it; 'Mezo' is kept as printed. Page 9 is blank apart from a 'Mark (of 4):' box; page footers 'Student number 1 4' are not transcribed. The Resource Booklet (Table 1, Maps 4–6) is not in the archive document. No solutions document in the archive.

problems.title: II. Transportation and Accessibility
problems.statement:
**II.2.** There is a plan to build a tunnel for cars in Belgrade from **A** to **B** (**Map 4**). Provide positive justifications (benefits) for building this tunnel for future development of tourism in Košutnjak Park. **(2 m)**

problems.title: IV. Potential and limitations for sustainable development of youth tourism at Košutnjak Park
problems.statement: **IV.1.** Using the Resource Booklet materials and your field observations from yesterday, think about kinds of youth tourism that could be practiced here. Provide answers to the following questions in the boxes, with brief explanation of reasons for each of them. **(4m)**

parts.label: A.
parts.statement: Which one of the already existing activities would you recommend to support and develop as a preference?

parts.label: B.
parts.statement: Which one of the already existing activities would you recommend to limit?

parts.label: C.
parts.statement: Which one completely new activity (never or very rarely practiced here before) would you recommend for development? Briefly describe it, informing title of activity, length of route, appropriate season of the year, and other important characteristics.
